desc:
A customer support assistant that hands off hard cases takes the repeated questions off your team and keeps people for the problems that need them. Ecom Swift LLC builds the assistant around your help content and past tickets, with safe handoff rules.

## What is an AI support assistant, and what should it handle?

A support assistant is a chat tool that answers customers' routine questions on your site or in your app, using your own policies and help content. It should handle the predictable material: shipping times, return steps, account access, how-to questions and opening hours. It should not handle disputes, sensitive situations or anything it cannot answer from your content.

The aim is not to replace your team. It is to stop skilled people from typing the same answer for the hundredth time, so they have time for the conversations that matter.

## Why repeated questions drain a support team

Most support inboxes follow a pattern. A small group of questions makes up most of the volume, and the rest are one-off cases. Staff answer the same few again and again, while the hard cases wait in the queue. Replies slow down, mistakes creep in and people get tired.

Customers feel the effect as slow answers, inconsistent advice and long waits on simple matters. An assistant that answers common questions at any hour gives them speed, and gives your team room to think about the cases that need care.

## How good support automation affects the business

When routine questions are answered accurately and instantly, fewer tickets reach your team, response times on difficult cases improve and staff can spend time on retention, not repetition. Accuracy is the condition. A fast wrong answer causes complaints, refunds and reputation damage.

That is why the design matters more than the technology. The assistant must know where its knowledge ends, say so, and pass the chat on with context. The outcome depends on your content, your volume and your policies, so we describe what the work improves rather than promising a number.

## What a dependable support assistant includes

- Coverage of your most frequent question types, written from your own policies.
- Answers that stay within your approved content and say so when unsure.
- A handoff to your inbox or helpdesk, with a short summary attached.
- Connections to tools such as Zendesk, Freshdesk or Gorgias where you use them.
- Rules for refunds, complaints and angry customers.
- Sensitive topics, such as legal threats or account security, that always go to a person.
- Different replies inside and outside working hours.
- Counts of chats resolved by the bot and chats passed to staff.
- Testing against real past tickets, not invented examples.
- A guide for your team on reading handoffs and updating answers.

## What we do

We begin by reading your help content and a sample of past tickets to learn which questions are most frequent and how your team answers them. From this we draft the question types the assistant will cover and the answers it will give, written from your own policies.

We then build the assistant and the handoff. The Basic package covers the top questions with email handoff. The Standard package covers many more question types, connects to a ticket tool, attaches a summary to each handed-off chat and sets rules for refunds and complaints. The Premium package covers the widest range, separates in-hours and out-of-hours behavior, counts resolved and handed-off chats and adds a launch check with a tuning round.

Before launch we run the assistant against past tickets and compare its answers with what your team sent. Wrong answers are fixed in the content or the rules, not left to chance. The assistant does not issue refunds on its own; money decisions stay with your staff.

## What to do, and what to avoid

**Do:**
- Start with the questions that fill most of your inbox.
- Decide in advance which topics always go to a person.
- Give the assistant a clear way to say "I am not sure."
- Read the handed-off chats weekly and add what is missing.
- Keep your policies in one place the assistant draws from.

**Avoid:**
- Letting the assistant guess when content is missing.
- Hiding the option to reach a person.
- Automating complaints and sensitive cases.
- Launching without testing on real tickets.
- Leaving old policies in the help content after they change.

## Who this service is for

This service suits a small business owner who answers the same emails every day. It suits an online store with seasonal peaks that overwhelm the inbox. It also suits a support team that already uses a helpdesk and wants routine tickets cleared before they arrive.

## What we need from you

Share your help content, policies and a set of past tickets or emails, with private details removed where possible. Tell us which topics need a person every time and where handoffs should go. We ask for access to your chatbot and helpdesk as a team member or collaborator. Passwords are never needed.
